title: Proper generic morphisms extend to a fibrewise dense big open
statement: Let $D$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one, with fraction field $E$, and let $T$ be a nonempty open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $X$ be an affine scheme smooth over $T$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $Y\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Write $X_E=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $Y_E=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-pc-base-change]. For every $E$-morphism $f_E:X_E\to Y_E$, there are an open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ and a $T$-morphism $v:V\to Y$ such that $V\times_T\operatorname{Spec}E=X_E$, $v_E=f_E$, and $V$ contains every point $x\in X$ satisfying $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\leq1$. Moreover $V_t$ is dense in $X_t$ for every $t\in T$, where $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $V_t=V\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. No group structure or smoothness on $Y$ is assumed.

proof.text: The empty source is settled by $V=\varnothing$. Otherwise $T$ is normal: its stalks are localizations of the normal domain $D$. Smooth normal ascent makes $X$ normal. Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation, hence local finite type. Since $T$ is locally Noetherian, so is $X$; since $X$ is affine it is Noetherian. Its underlying space is therefore Noetherian (a finite union of spectra of Noetherian rings), and so is every subspace; hence $X$ and each of its quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components. By the normal-components lemma, $X$ is the disjoint union of its finitely many clopen irreducible components $C$, each an integral scheme with integrally closed local rings. The structure map $a:X\to T$ is open. Therefore every nonempty open $W\subseteq C$ meets $X_E$: the nonempty open $a(W)$ of the integral scheme $T$ contains its generic point. In particular $C_E$ is nonempty and dense in $C$, and the generic point $\eta_C$ of $C$ lies over the generic point of $T$ (otherwise its image would be a closed singleton, whereas $a(C)$ is open).

source.place: Tag 034F (lemma-normal-local-smooth); with Properties Tag 0357 and Morphisms Tags 01T6, 01UA

proof.text: Fix a component $C$ and put $K=k(C)$. The canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to C$ factors through $C_E$, since $\eta_C$ lies over the generic point of $T$. Compose with $f_E$ to obtain a $T$-morphism $b_C:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$. For any $z\in C_E$, the canonical morphism $c_z:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,z}\to X$ factors through $X_E$ (with $c_\eta:\operatorname{Spec}E\to T$ the canonical morphism at $\eta$): by the bijection between morphisms from the spectrum of a local ring and pairs (point, local homomorphism), $a\circ c_z$ and $c_\eta\circ\operatorname{Spec}(a^\sharp_z)$ both correspond to $(\eta,a^\sharp_z:\mathcal O_{T,\eta}=E\to\mathcal O_{X,z})$, so they are equal, and the fibre-product property gives the factorization. Composing with $f_E$ gives $\varphi_z:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,z}\to Y$. Its restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is $b_C$, using the canonical fraction-field identification for stalks of an integral scheme.

source.place: Tag 0BX6, lemma-morphism-defined-local-ring, setup of the local spreading argument

proof.text: For each $x\in C\setminus C_E$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\leq1$, put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. It is a Noetherian normal local domain. Its dimension is not zero: a zero-dimensional local domain is a field, so $x$ would be the generic point of $C$, which is already in $C_E$. Thus $\dim A=1$, and the one-dimensional normal local ring theorem makes $A$ a discrete valuation ring, in particular a valuation ring. Its fraction field is canonically $K$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ is the canonical morphism of $C$ at $\eta_C$, since both send the point to $\eta_C$ and induce the identity of $\mathcal O_{X,\eta_C}=K$ (part (2) of the canonical-morphism lemma at the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$), hence agree under the local-spectrum bijection; so the square over $T$ commutes. Apply the proper valuative existence criterion to $b_C:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ and the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$. It gives a $T$-morphism $\varphi_x:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ restricting to $b_C$.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, (5) implies (1); valuative step in BLR 1.2 Proposition 8, printed p.15

proof.text: Apply local-ring spreading to every $\varphi_z$ of step 2 and every $\varphi_x$ of step 3. The source is locally Noetherian, and $Y\to T$ is locally of finite type because it is proper. We obtain an open neighbourhood $W_p\subseteq C$ of each selected point $p$ and a $T$-morphism $h_p:W_p\to Y$ whose pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,p}$ is $\varphi_p$. Its pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is therefore $b_C$. On $(W_p)_E$, compare $(h_p)_E$ with $f_E|_{(W_p)_E}$. This source is integral: on affine charts its rings are localizations of domains, with fraction field $K$. Their maps agree after the dense generic-point morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to(W_p)_E$. The relative separated-target equality theorem gives equality on $(W_p)_E$. Here properness supplies separatedness over $T$; the comparison is made over $T$, so absolute separatedness of $Y$ is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 0BX6, lemma-morphism-defined-local-ring, (2)(c); Schemes Tag 01KM for equality

proof.text: On an overlap $W_p\cap W_q$ inside the same component, both morphisms restrict on its generic fibre to $f_E$, by step 4. If the overlap is nonempty, its generic fibre has dense image in it by step 1. The overlap is reduced, being open in an integral component. The relative separated-target equality theorem applied to this dense-image morphism gives $h_p|_{W_p\cap W_q}=h_q|_{W_p\cap W_q}$. Empty overlaps require no argument, and opens in distinct components are disjoint. Glue the $h_p$ to a morphism $v:V\to Y$ on $V=\bigcup_pW_p$. Their structure-map equalities glue as well, so $v$ is over $T$. By construction $V$ contains all of $X_E$ and every point with local dimension at most one; step 4 gives $v_E=f_E$ and $V_E=X_E$.

source.place: Tag 01KM, lemma-where-are-they-equal; open-cover gluing of morphisms

proof.text: It remains to check density in each closed fibre. Fix a point $t\in T$ other than the generic point $\eta$; since $D$ is a one-dimensional domain, $t$ is a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_t$ of $D$. Fix a generic point $\xi$ of an irreducible component of $X_t$. The local ring $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}=D_{\mathfrak m_t}$ is a discrete valuation ring; choose a uniformizer $\pi$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$, a Noetherian local ring. The fibre-stalk quotient identifies $A/\pi A$ with $\mathcal O_{X_t,\xi}$. The latter has only one prime ideal: $\xi$ is a generic point, so it has no proper generalizations in the fibre, and the canonical local spectrum has precisely those generalizations as image. Consequently the maximal ideal of $A$ is the only prime containing $\pi$, hence is minimal over $(\pi)$. Krull's principal ideal height bound gives height at most one. The localization dimension formula identifies this height with $\dim A$, so $\xi\in V$ by step 5.

For $t\neq\eta$, step 6 puts every component generic point of $X_t$ in $V_t$. The closure of $V_t$ therefore contains each irreducible component, and hence is all of $X_t$. For the generic point $t=\eta$, $V_t=X_t$ by step 5. These exhaust the points of $T$, since $D$ is a one-dimensional domain. Empty fibres satisfy density automatically. This proves the final clause without any group structure or smoothness on the proper target.

source.place: Elementary closure argument after the principal ideal height bound
